_note: Clip L1 (docs/specs/social-l1-clips.md, chủ 11/11): giáo viên Ama/Carlos nói tiếng Anh ≤B1 ≤150 wpm; chữ bản địa (native.*) = bản tay tầng i18n-fixed (docs/I18N-PIPELINE.md), {m:từ} lấy nghĩa từ kho từ (vi) / web/packs/<lang>.json, kiểm bằng scripts/rig/native-qa.mjs. lang = cfg.lang của page (D1 yt_chan_cfg): clip lang=X chỉ lên page lang=X.

in.why: With he, she, it, add s to the verb.
in.answer_say: Drinks! He drinks tea every day.

native.hook: Người Việt hay quên âm “s” này!
native.tip: Với he/she/it, động từ phải thêm -s. Tiếng Việt không chia động từ nên rất dễ quên.
native.caption: Bạn có hay nói “She like coffee.” không? 😅 Với he/she/it, động từ phải thêm -s: “She likes coffee.” Nghe cô Ama đọc rồi lặp lại nhé! Luyện thêm ngữ pháp trong app Lexkite.
native.comment: Đáp án: “drinks”. Nhớ thêm -s sau he/she/it nhé! Luyện thêm bài ngữ pháp miễn phí tại đây: {link}

en.tip: With he/she/it, the verb needs -s. Many learners forget it because the verb never changes in their own language.
en.caption: Do you often say this? “She like coffee.” With he/she/it, the verb needs -s: “She likes coffee.” Listen to Ama read it, then repeat! Practice more grammar in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Very does not go before a verb.
in.answer_say: Very much! I like pizza very much.

native.tip: Tiếng Việt nói “rất thích”, nhưng tiếng Anh phải nói “like … very much”.
native.caption: Bạn có nói “I very like music.” không? 🙈 Người bản xứ nói “I like music very much.” Nghe Ama đọc rồi lặp lại theo nhé! Luyện thêm cách nói tự nhiên trong app Lexkite.
native.comment: Đáp án: “very much”. Thử đặt một câu về món bạn thích nhất, rồi luyện thêm miễn phí tại đây: {link}

en.tip: Learners say “very like”, but in English you must say “like … very much.”
en.caption: Do you say this? “I very like music.” Native speakers say “I like music very much.” Listen to Ama read it, then repeat after her! Practice more natural phrases in the Lexkite app.

in.why: For age, use am, not have.
in.memory: Age: I am, not I have.
in.answer_say: Is! She is twenty years old.

native.tip: Em inglês, para falar a idade usamos “I am”, não “I have”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I have twenty years.” O certo é “I am twenty years old.” Ouça o Carlos falar e repita com ele! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “is”. Em inglês a idade usa o verbo ser. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, to say your age we use “I am”, not “I have”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I have twenty years.” The right way is “I am twenty years old.” Listen to Carlos say it and repeat with him! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I pretend to travel next year.
in.right: I plan to travel next year.
in.why: Pretend means to act like something is true.
in.answer_say: Plan! I plan to study more.

native.tip: “Pretend” em inglês significa fingir. Para dizer que você pretende fazer algo, use “plan”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este falso cognato! 😬 Muita gente diz “I pretend to travel next year.” O certo é “I plan to travel next year.” “Pretend” quer dizer fingir, e “pretender” é “plan”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “plan”. Anote esta frase e treine outros falsos cognatos com um quiz grátis: {link}

en.tip: “Pretend” in English means to fake. To say you intend to do something, use “plan”.
en.caption: Watch out for this false friend! Many people say “I pretend to travel next year.” The right way is “I plan to travel next year.” “Pretend” means to fake, and “pretender” means “plan”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: With hungry, thirsty, and cold, use am.
in.answer_say: Am! I am thirsty.

native.tip: En inglés no “tenemos” hambre: decimos “I am hungry.” Pasa igual con sed y frío.
native.caption: ¿Tú también dices “I have hunger”? 😅 En español “tengo hambre”, pero en inglés usamos “to be”: “I am hungry.” ¡Escucha a Ama y repite con ella! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “am”. Con hambre, sed y frío usamos el verbo “to be”. Practica más con un quiz gratis aquí: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I have hunger”? No!
en.tip: In English we do not “have” hunger: we say “I am hungry.” The same goes for thirst and cold.
en.caption: Do you also say “I have hunger”? Learners say “tengo hambre”, but English uses “to be”: “I am hungry.” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Agree is already a verb. Do not add am.
in.answer_say: Agrees! She agrees with me.

native.tip: “Agree” ya es un verbo, así que no necesitas “am”. Se dice “I agree.”
native.caption: En español decimos “estoy de acuerdo”, pero en inglés no se dice “I am agree”. 🙈 Lo correcto es “I agree with you.” ¡Escucha a Ama y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “agrees”. Recuerda: sin “am”, solo “agree”. Practica más con un quiz gratis aquí: {link}

en.tip: “Agree” is already a verb, so you do not need “am”. You say “I agree.”
en.caption: Learners say “estoy de acuerdo”, but in English you do not say “I am agree”. The right way is “I agree with you.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: I would like a coffee, please.
in.why: Become means to start to be. It is not get.
in.answer_say: Like! I would like a tea, please.

native.tip: „Become“ bedeutet „werden“. Wenn Sie etwas bestellen, sagen Sie „I would like“.
native.caption: Vorsicht, falscher Freund! 😬 “Become” heißt auf Deutsch {m:become}, nicht „bekommen“. Beim Bestellen sagen Sie “I would like a coffee, please”. Hören Sie Carlos zu und sprechen Sie nach!
native.comment: Lösung: “like”. Beim Bestellen sagen Sie immer „I would like“. Mehr falsche Freunde üben Sie hier kostenlos: {link}

en.tip: “Become” means “werden”. When you order something, you say “I would like”.
en.caption: Careful, false friend! “Become” means werden, not “bekommen”. When ordering, you say “I would like a coffee, please”. Listen to Carlos and repeat!

in.wrong: I live here since two years.
in.right: I have lived here for two years.
in.why: Use for with a length of time.

quiz.stem: I have worked here ___ three years.

in.answer_say: For! I have worked here for three years.

native.tip: Für eine Zeitdauer wie „zwei Jahre“ nehmen Sie „for“ und die Zeitform „have lived“.
native.caption: Sagen Sie auch “I live here since two years”? 🙈 Im Englischen heißt es “I have lived here for two years”. Hören Sie Carlos zu und sprechen Sie nach! Mehr üben in der Lexkite-App.
native.comment: Lösung: “for”. Für eine Zeitdauer nehmen Sie „for“, für einen Startpunkt „since“. Üben Sie mehr mit einem kostenlosen Quiz: {link}

en.tip: For a length of time like “two years” you use “for” and the tense “have lived”.
en.caption: Do you also say “I live here since two years”? In English it is “I have lived here for two years”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to the library to buy books.
in.right: I go to the bookstore to buy books.
in.why: A library lends books. A bookstore sells them.
in.answer_say: Bookstore! I buy books at the bookstore.

native.tip: « Library » veut dire {m:library}. Pour acheter des livres, allez dans « a bookstore ».
native.caption: Vous dites “I go to the library to buy books.” ? Attention, faux ami ! « Library » signifie {m:library}, pas librairie. Dites plutôt “I go to the bookstore to buy books.” — écoutez Ama et répétez avec elle ! Plus d’exercices dans l’appli Lexkite.
native.comment: Réponse : “bookstore” — Une bibliothèque prête des livres, une librairie les vend. Testez d’autres pièges avec un quiz gratuit : {link}

en.tip: A “library” lends books. To buy a book, go to “a bookstore.”
en.caption: Do you say this? “I go to the library to buy books.” Watch out, false friend! A library lends books; it does not sell them. Say “I go to the bookstore to buy books.” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! More exercises in the Lexkite app.

in.why: For age, use am, not have.
in.memory: Age: I am, not I have.
in.answer_say: Is! He is twenty years old.

native.tip: En anglais, on n’« a » pas un âge : on dit “I am twenty years old”.
native.caption: Vous dites “I have twenty years.” ? En anglais, l’âge se dit avec “be”. Dites plutôt “I am twenty years old.” — écoutez Ama et répétez avec elle ! Plus d’exercices dans l’appli Lexkite.
native.comment: Réponse : “is” — En anglais, l’âge se dit avec le verbe être. Testez d’autres pièges avec un quiz gratuit : {link}

en.tip: In English, you do not “have” an age: you say “I am twenty years old”.
en.caption: Do you say this? “I have twenty years.” In English, age uses “be”. Say “I am twenty years old.” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! More exercises in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Bored is how you feel. Boring is how a thing is.
in.memory: I am bored. The movie is boring.
in.answer_say: Boring! The movie is boring.

native.tip: 「boring」は退屈なもの、「bored」は退屈な気持ち。自分の気持ちは bored！
native.caption: “I am boring.”と言っていませんか？😅 これだと “I am a dull person.” つまり「私はつまらない人」という意味になります。気持ちを言うときは “I am bored.” が正解です。Amaの声を聞いてまねしてみよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“boring”。映画や物には boring を使います。無料クイズで続きを練習しよう：{link}

en.tip: “Boring” describes a thing, “bored” describes your feeling. For your feeling, say bored!
en.caption: Do you say this? “I am boring.” 😅 That means “I am a dull person.” To say how you feel, say “I am bored.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.right: There are four people in my family.
in.why: Use there are, then say the number.
in.memory: There are four people in my family.
in.answer_say: There are! There are five people in my family.

native.tip: 「My family is four people」は不自然。人数は “There are ~ people in my family” と言います。
native.caption: 「家族は4人です」を “My family is four people.” と言っていませんか？🙈 自然な英語は “There are four people in my family.” です。Carlosの声をまねして練習しよう！Lexkiteアプリでもっと練習できます。
native.comment: 答え：“There are”。人数を言うときの形を覚えよう。無料クイズで練習：{link}

en.tip: “My family is four people” sounds odd. Say “There are four people in my family.”
en.caption: Do you say this? “My family is four people.” 🙈 The natural way is “There are four people in my family.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: We say make a mistake.
in.answer_say: Made! She made a mistake.

native.tip: 실수는 do가 아니라 make! 이렇게 말해요 👉 “I made a mistake.”
native.caption: “I did a mistake”라고 말하고 있진 않나요? 😅 영어에서는 실수를 “do”(하다)가 아니라 “make”(만들다)를 써요. 맞는 문장 ✅ “I made a mistake.” Carlos 선생님 발음을 듣고 따라 해 보세요! Lexkite 앱에서 더 연습해요.
native.comment: 정답: “made”! 실수는 make a mistake! 무료 퀴즈로 더 연습해 보세요: {link}

en.tip: For a mistake, use make, not do! Say “I made a mistake.”
en.caption: Do you say “I did a mistake” in English? 😅 In English you “make” a mistake, so “I made a mistake” is right. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Do not use to before home.
in.answer_say: Home! I want to go home now.

native.tip: home 앞에는 to를 쓰지 않아요. 이렇게 말해요 👉 “I will go home.”
native.caption: “I will go to home”처럼 말하고 있나요? 🙈 home 앞에는 to가 필요 없어요. 자연스러운 문장 ✅ “I will go home.” Ama 선생님을 따라 말해 보세요! Lexkite 앱에서 더 연습해요.
native.comment: 정답: “home”! go home처럼 to 없이 써요! 무료 퀴즈로 연습해 보세요: {link}

en.tip: Do not put “to” before home. “I will go home” is right.
en.caption: Do you say “I will go to home” in English? 🙈 You do not need “to” before home. “I will go home” sounds natural. Repeat with Ama! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Yesterday means the past. Use went.
in.answer_say: Went! Yesterday she went to work.

native.tip: 英语动词要随时间变化：昨天用 “went”，不是 “go”。
native.caption: 你是不是也会说这句？“Yesterday I go to school.”😅 英语里说过去的事，动词要变成过去式：“Yesterday I went to school.”跟着 Ama 老师读一读吧！在 Lexkite 应用里练习更多。
native.comment: 答案：“went”，说昨天的事要用过去式！用免费测验继续练习：{link}

en.tip: English verbs change with time: after yesterday use “went”, not “go.”
en.caption: Do you say this? “Yesterday I go to school.” 😅 In English, past events need a past verb: “Yesterday I went to school.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Open is for doors. For lights, turn on.
in.answer_say: Turn on! Please turn on the music.

native.tip: open 用来开门；开灯、开音乐要用 “turn on”。
native.caption: 你会说这句吗？“Please open the light.”🙈 在英语里 open 是开门、开盖子，开灯要说 “Please turn on the light.”跟着 Carlos 老师读一读！在 Lexkite 应用里练习更多。
native.comment: 答案：“turn on”，开灯、开音乐都用 turn on！免费测验在这里：{link}

en.tip: Open is for doors. For lights and music, use “turn on.”
en.caption: Do you say this? “Please open the light.” 🙈 In English, open is for doors and lids. For a light, say “Please turn on the light.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Use have for things you own.
in.memory: I have, not I am having.
in.answer_say: Has! She has a big house.

native.tip: अपने पास कुछ होने के लिए “I have” बोलें, “I am having” नहीं।
native.caption: क्या आप भी कहते हैं “I am having two brothers”? 😅 अंग्रेज़ी में “I have two brothers” सही है, क्योंकि पास होने या रिश्ते बताने वाले have के साथ -ing नहीं लगता। Ama की आवाज़ सुनकर दोहराइए! Lexkite ऐप में और अभ्यास करें।
native.comment: उत्तर: “has”। अपने पास कुछ होने या रिश्ते बताने के लिए have बोलें। मुफ़्त क्विज़ यहाँ करें: {link}

en.tip: To say you own something, say I have instead of I am having here.
en.caption: Do you say “I am having two brothers”? 😅 In English “I have two brothers” is right, because have for owning or family does not take -ing. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Just say name. Good name sounds strange.
in.answer_say: Name! What is your name?

native.tip: हिंदी में “आपका शुभ नाम” चलता है, पर अंग्रेज़ी में बस “What is your name?” बोलें।
native.caption: क्या आप “What is your good name?” पूछते हैं? 🙈 अंग्रेज़ी में “good” नहीं लगता — सीधे “What is your name?” पूछिए। Carlos की आवाज़ सुनकर दोहराइए! Lexkite ऐप में और अभ्यास करें।
native.comment: उत्तर: “name”। “good name” हटा दें और सीधे पूछें। मुफ़्त क्विज़ यहाँ: {link}

en.tip: Some learners add good to be polite, but in English just ask “What is your name?”
en.caption: Do you ask “What is your good name?” 🙈 English does not need “good” here — just ask “What is your name?” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Do not use am before a verb like go.
in.memory: I go. Not I am go.
in.answer_say: Goes! She goes to work every day.

native.tip: لا نضع am قبل الفعل: نقول “I go to school.” وليس “I am go”
native.caption: هل تقول أحيانًا هذه الجملة؟ “I am go to school” 😅 في الإنجليزية لا نستخدم am قبل الفعل، فالجملة الصحيحة “I go to school.” استمع إلى Ama وكرّر معها! تدرّب أكثر في تطبيق Lexkite.
native.comment: الإجابة: “goes” — لا تضع am أو is قبل الفعل العادي. تدرّب مع اختبار مجاني هنا: {link}

en.tip: We do not put am before a verb: say “I go to school”, not “I am go”
en.caption: Do you sometimes say this? “I am go to school” 😅 In English we do not use am before the verb, so the right sentence is “I go to school.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: In a question, put are before you.
in.answer_say: Are you! Where are you from?

native.tip: في السؤال نضع الفعل قبل الفاعل: “Where are you going?” وليس “Where you are going?”
native.caption: هل تسأل “Where you are going?” 🙈 في الإنجليزية يأتي الفعل are قبل you في السؤال: “Where are you going?” استمع إلى Carlos وكرّر معه! تدرّب أكثر في تطبيق Lexkite.
native.comment: الإجابة: “are you” — تذكّر: الفعل قبل الفاعل في السؤال. اختبار مجاني هنا: {link}

en.tip: In a question, the verb comes before the subject: “Where are you going?” not “Where you are going?”
en.caption: Do you ask “Where you are going?” 🙈 In English, are comes before you in a question: “Where are you going?” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Use tell before a person.
in.answer_say: Tell! Can you tell me the time?

native.tip: Bir kişiye bir şey söylerken “tell” kullanılır: “Please tell me the way.”
native.caption: “Please say me the way” mi diyorsun? 😅 İngilizcede kişiden önce “tell” gelir, doğrusu “Please tell me the way.” Ama’yı dinle ve tekrar et! Lexkite uygulamasında daha çok pratik yap.
native.comment: Cevap: “tell”. Bir kişiye bir şey söylerken tell kullan. Ücretsiz testle pratik yap: {link}

en.tip: Use “tell” before a person: “Please tell me the way.”
en.caption: Do you say “Please say me the way”? 😅 In English “tell” goes before the person, so it is “Please tell me the way.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Passed means you did well.

quiz.stem: I studied hard and ___ the test.

in.answer_say: Passed! I studied hard and passed the test.

native.tip: Türkçede “sınavı verdim” deriz ama İngilizcede “I passed the exam” denir.
native.caption: “I gave the exam yesterday” mi diyorsun? 🙈 Sınavı geçtiysen İngilizcede “passed” denir. Doğrusu “I passed the exam yesterday.” Carlos’u dinle ve tekrar et! Lexkite uygulamasında daha çok pratik yap.
native.comment: Cevap: “passed”. Sınavı geçtiysen passed de. Ücretsiz testle pratik yap: {link}

en.tip: If you did well on a test, say “passed”: “I passed the exam.”
en.caption: Do you say “I gave the exam yesterday”? 🙈 If you did well, English says “passed”. The right sentence is “I passed the exam yesterday.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: Ask about age the right way!
in.why: For age, ask how old.
in.answer_say: Old! How old is your brother?

native.tip: «Сколько тебе лет?» — по-английски “How old are you?”
native.caption: Ты тоже спрашиваешь “How many years are you”? 😅 По-русски «сколько тебе лет», но по-английски возраст спрашивают так: “How old are you?” Послушай Ама и повтори за ней! Больше практики — в приложении Lexkite.
native.comment: Ответ: “old”. Возраст в английском — это how old. Бесплатный тест для практики здесь: {link}

en.hook: Ask about age the right way!
en.tip: For age, ask: “How old are you?”
en.caption: Do you also ask “How many years are you”? 😅 For age, English asks: “How old are you?” Listen to Ama and repeat with her! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.why: Use to for a place you go to.
in.answer_say: To! We went to the park.

native.tip: Куда-то едешь — говори “to”: “I went to Spain.”
native.caption: Ты говоришь “I went in Spain”? 🙈 По-русски «в Испанию», но по-английски нужно “to”. Правильно: “I went to Spain.” Послушай Карлоса и повтори! Больше практики — в приложении Lexkite.
native.comment: Ответ: “to”. Куда идём — to. Бесплатный тест для практики здесь: {link}

en.tip: When you go somewhere, say “to”: “I went to Spain.”
en.caption: Do you say “I went in Spain”? 🙈 When you go somewhere, English needs a small word: to. Correct: “I went to Spain.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
